evidence.note: Claim: the swarm schedulers item-level ordering (critical-path first, then longest-waiting queue term) can express as a second Optimizer adapter over the ports one cut, reading per-candidate facts from an open ctx filled only for the keys the adapter declares (greedy-v1 declares none). Refutation: greedy-v1 order pins or the golden snapshots would change; swarm order not critical-first. Probe: python test_adapter_optimizer.py 12 passed, test_plan_pipeline test_schedule_offer test_flowsignals test_progress_line test_swarm_score test_schedule_model test_metrics 236 passed, default greedy order unchanged ([b,d,a,c]). CONFIRMED

Rules r-adapters, r-small-files, r-everything-configurable, D-extension-contract-answers read. swarm-v1 added as a second adapter of the existing Optimizer port (no new port, no third-party, no shared-file edit); files under 20KB (optimizer.py 10.2KB, _plan.py 15.3KB); [schedule].optimizer knob already validates name in OPTIMIZERS so swarm-v1 is selectable via file/CLI/MCP; deterministic (id tie-break). ctx is the open per-candidate facts map (critical, waited_s).

swarm-v1 second Optimizer adapter (order: critical path then longest-waiting then greedy terms then id; cut inherited from GreedyV1; reads ctx facts); _plan._facts populates ctx with per-candidate critical/waited_s only for the adapters declared facts; flowsignals/metrics-grid/progress_line route through plan()->get_optimizer (the port), not api.plan_for (layering). +5 tests pass; whole-suite affected tests pass; default greedy order byte-identical.

chunk_findings.detail: The only item marked critical is also the only item with waited_s > 0 (`a`: critical=True, waited_s=10; b/c/d have no facts). Both “critical then waited” and “waited then critical” therefore yield `["a", "b", "d", "c"]`, and the reverse-input assert repeats the same order. Input that would expose a swapped key — `q` critical=True waited_s=0 versus `p` critical=False waited_s=1000 — is never run, so a scorer that ranks longest wait ahead of the critical path still passes every swarm test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapter_optimizer.py:test_swarm_orders_critical_then_waited_then_priority_then_id

chunk_findings.detail: `explain` is only called after `order({}, [_c("b", True, 50)])`, so the assertion only locks the zero defaults (`critical=0, waited_s=0.0`). A scorer that hardcodes those zeros and never reads `facts` still satisfies `startswith`. No input with critical=True or a non-zero waited_s is explained, so the test does not check the promise in its name.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapter_optimizer.py:test_swarm_explain_itemises_critical_and_wait

chunk_findings.detail: `_facts` is passed straight in as the optimizer `ctx` (`cut(_facts(...), ...)` and `order(_facts(...), ...)`), and it returns a map keyed by item id. The same change’s adapter doc says the caller fills `ctx["facts"]` and that an adapter reads keys it knows from that entry. A `swarm-v1` (or any adapter) that follows the documented contract and reads `ctx["facts"][item_id]` gets a missing key: given ready item `T1`, `ctx` is `{"T1": {"critical": ..., "waited_s": ...}}`, so `ctx["facts"]` is absent and critical-path / wait ordering never sees the facts. The function docstring claims the same `facts` entry and then returns the bare id map.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/schedule/_plan.py:_facts

chunk_findings.detail: The port contract in this diff still says the optimizer is deterministic with “no clock”, while `_facts` injects `waited_s = now - epoch(created_at)` and the new `swarm-v1` adapter is documented as ordering by longest wait. Two ready items filed 10s apart therefore change relative rank as wall time moves, so the “no clock / integer tie-break only” promise is false for the adapter this change adds.
